quote: You do not have to be good. / You do not have to walk on your knees / for a hundred miles through the desert repenting. / You only have to let the soft animal of your body / love what it loves.
source: Mary Oliver, Wild Geese, lines 1 to 5, Dream Work (Atlantic Monthly Press, 1986), p. 14

evidence.where: Two independent reprints crediting Dream Work (Atlantic Monthly Press, 1986), both printing the third line without a comma before repenting; a later printing reproduced in Poetry for Students adds the comma. Page 14 confirmed by a search across dealer listings. Poetry Foundation and the Library of Congress pages refused the fetch.
evidence.edition: Dream Work, The Atlantic Monthly Press, 1986, p. 14
evidence.locator: Wild Geese, lines 1 to 5, the opening

reason: The five opening lines match the Dream Work text as reprinted by two sources crediting that edition; the only variant in circulation is a comma before repenting in later printings, and the Dream Work wording is the one shipped. Not shipped, person at zero of three, not banned.
